research.name: Outcome-Aware Fine-Tuning of Vision-Language Models for Web Agents
highlights: Ran a controlled study isolating outcome supervision for web agents: LoRA fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-8B on 6,445 matched Multimodal Mind2Web examples, nearly doubling Step Success Rate over the zero-shot baseline (31.99% to 62.32%).

Showed that adding structured page-transition labels to the training target gave no measurable gain over action-only SFT (task-level 95% CIs overlap), a null result that replicated across all three test splits.

Traced the regression to a terminal-action bias (predicting a child click over the parent hover) through dataset, schema, and failure-case analysis, supported by AXTree and chain-of-thought ablations.

research.name: Cross-Lingual Hallucination Detection in Multilingual LLMs
highlights: Tested whether correctness probes trained only on English hidden states of Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct can flag hallucinations zero-shot in Chinese, Thai, Vietnamese, and Indonesian; best probe reached 0.704 AUC on English and 0.64 to 0.68 across target languages with no target-language supervision.

Ran a full 28-layer sweep across six probe families and two extraction points, showing post-answer features and deeper layers transfer best and that the correctness signal is low-dimensional (random forests within 0.01 AUC of the MLP).

Traced the dominant failure to confident hallucinations the hidden state does not expose, and to conflating knowledge absence with hallucination, motivating a three-way correct/uncertain/hallucinating labeling scheme.

research.name: PRISM: Probing Routed Information Flow via Structured Multimodal Bottlenecks
highlights: Designed and validated a hierarchical fusion variant outperforming the symmetric design by +2.7% (Acc2/F1); identified that asymmetric (AV/VA) fusion matches symmetric performance with fewer parameters, a key insight for production multimodal model design.
Researched fusion efficiency in multimodal models; discovered that scaling fusion capacity (4 to 12 tokens) on CMU-MOSEI/MOSI hurts performance (-6% correlation), revealing architectural waste.

research.name: ScleraNext: Lightweight CNN Segmentation for Real-Time Biometric Identification
highlights: Optimized a production iris/retinal segmentation pipeline: replaced a cascaded 2-stage segmentation CNN with a single compact model, reducing inference latency by 73% for edge deployment.
Benchmarked YOLO, U-Net, MobileNet, and DenseNet on accuracy/latency tradeoffs and selected an optimized U-Net-based model.

research.name: GraphAct: Graph-Structured Action Prediction for Web Agents
highlights: Identified element grounding, not action prediction, as the core failure mode on Multimodal Mind2Web, then fused a DOM graph attention network into a frozen Qwen3-VL-8B backbone via a gated cross-attention adapter and LoRA, all within a single 24GB GPU.

Lifted element accuracy from 12.7% (no graph) to 49.5% and beat the strongest multimodal baseline by ~12 points with step accuracy reaching ~41%; showed these gains did not fully reach task success (7.75%) due to error accumulation over long trajectories.
Traced fixation and anchor-bias failures to the static per-step graph and fragile node pruning, and proposed dynamic node masking and topology-aware retention as fixes.

projects.name: ZulipGPT: LLM Integration for Chat Summarization in Open-Source Messaging
highlights: Shipped chat and inbox summarization into the Zulip open-source codebase with topic-drift detection and citation-backed prompts to reduce hallucination and injection risk.

Built a deterministic identity-masking pipeline using keyed pseudonym mapping before inference, providing a stronger privacy guarantee than post-hoc PII filtering since the model never sees real identities.
Cut summarization latency to under 15s via trigger-based invocation, rolling context windows, and message batching.

projects.name: Real-Time Movie Recommendation Platform
highlights: Trained an SVD collaborative filtering model on ~200K Kafka interactions; deployed a Flask API (<50ms latency) with Docker and automated retraining every 3 days. Designed a hybrid cold-start solution achieving 85%+ coverage on new users.

Built an end-to-end data pipeline (schema validation, drift detection, offline/online evaluation: NDCG@10 0.52, HR@10 0.68) with CI/CD testing (82% coverage). Set up a monitoring dashboard tracking >99% availability, model accuracy, costs, and data drift.
Designed A/B testing infrastructure, experimented, and found the cold-start strategy lifts NDCG@10 by 8%.

projects.name: SteelRAG: Hybrid Sparse-Dense Retrieval over a Crawled Local Knowledge Corpus
highlights: Built a 5,334-document corpus from 20+ sources via three targeted scraping rounds guided by gap analysis of ~117 unanswered question clusters; corpus expansion alone drove a +6.8% absolute gain in a combined F1 and LLM-judge score.
Implemented BM25 (bm25s), FAISS (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 384-dim), and Reciprocal Rank Fusion from scratch; hybrid RRF outperformed dense-only by +4.46% across F1, Recall, ROUGE-L, and LLM Judge.

Deployed Qwen2-7B-Instruct on a Modal A10G GPU; batch embedding cut index build from 3 hours to under 15 minutes, and reducing chunk size from 200 to 100 words improved F1 by +1.40% with no recall loss.
